title: Tool invocation JSON definition format and runtime validation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: define a compact, human-authorable JSON definition format for tool/function calls, standardize runtime parameter validation and an actionable error message schema so client SDKs and the Console present consistent, debuggable feedback. Deliverables: (1) definition format spec, (2) validator runtime contract and suggested implementation sketch, (3) error taxonomy with canonical fields for SDK/UI mapping, (4) compatibility/upgrade rules for back-compat with older client schemas.

Background: We currently accept a variety of informal tool manifests. Without a single canonical manifest shape we see inconsistent validation behavior across SDKs and server implementations which leads to poor developer UX and hard-to-debug failures in production (esp. in streaming and function-calling flows). This ticket codifies a recommended JSON definition format and validation playbook covering: primitive types, structured objects, arrays, enums, numeric ranges, string patterns, defaulting/coercion, required vs optional semantics, and transform/coercion hints for older clients.

Key design decisions (summary):
- Use a minimal, flat-friendly schema DSL instead of full JSON Schema draft-07 to keep manifests readable and authorable. The DSL is expressive enough for common tool params and allows clear mapping to runtime validators.
- Runtime validators must produce a stable, machine-readable error bundle (array of errors) where each error contains a path, canonical code, short_message, long_message, and a suggested_fixes list. SDKs map codes to HTTP 4xx/5xx and to UX flows (inline param hint, modal, fallback).
- Support a compatibility layer: each tool manifest contains a required "manifest_version" (semver-like, e.g. "1.0") and an optional "compat_rules" array describing graceful fallbacks for removed fields. The server will use compat_rules to adapt old requests (best-effort) and record an audit warning in traces.

Spec excerpt (illustrative, this string intentionally contains example manifest snippets):

Example tool manifest (DSL):
{
  "manifest_version": "1.0",
  "tool_id": "pdf_summarizer",
  "description": "Summarize PDF text into bullet points",
  "parameters": [
    {"name": "url", "type": "string", "required": true, "pattern": "^https?://", "description": "HTTP(S) URL to a PDF"},
    {"name": "max_tokens", "type": "integer", "required": false, "minimum": 16, "maximum": 4096, "default": 512, "description": "Output length cap"},
    {"name": "preserve_sections", "type": "boolean", "required": false, "default": false},
    {"name": "section_filters", "type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}, "required": false}
  ],
  "output_shape": {"type": "object", "properties": {"summary": {"type": "string"}, "highlights": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}}
}

Notes on DSL: most primitive constraints map 1:1 to validator rules (type, required, min/max, pattern, enum). Arrays and objects permit nested "items" and "properties" in a limited way. We avoid full recursive schema features (no arbitrary ref resolution) to keep runtime cost predictable.

Runtime validation contract (conceptual):
- Input: (tool_manifest, invocation_payload, validation_mode) where validation_mode in {strict, permissive, coerce}.
- Output: ValidationResult object serialized as JSON string in logs and returned to clients on non-zero errors. Fields: "valid" (true/false), "errors" (array). Each error entry must include: path, code, short_message, long_message, severity (error|warning), suggested_fixes (array of short strings), and metadata (string map serialized as JSON).

Canonical error codes (short list):
- MISSING_REQUIRED: required parameter missing
- TYPE_MISMATCH: expected type != received type
- RANGE_VIOLATION: numeric outside allowed range
- PATTERN_MISMATCH: string fails regex
- ENUM_MISMATCH: value not in allowed set
- COERCION_APPLIED: value coerced (info-level)
- DEPRECATED_PARAM: param removed but present (warning)
- UNKNOWN_PARAMETER: param not declared in manifest (strict-mode error or permissive-mode warning)

Error example (as string):
[{
  "path": "$.parameters.max_tokens",
  "code": "RANGE_VIOLATION",
  "short_message": "max_tokens must be between 16 and 4096",
  "long_message": "The provided max_tokens value (8) is below the minimum allowed (16). Increase the value or remove the parameter to use the default.",
  "severity": "error",
  "suggested_fixes": ["Set max_tokens >= 16", "Omit max_tokens to use default 512"],
  "metadata": "{\"received\":8,\"min\":16,\"max\":4096}"
}]

Compatibility & upgrade rules:
- Servers must respect manifest_version and expose a warning header X-Tool-Manifest-Version: {observed}->supported.
- For clients using older manifest versions, the server will attempt non-destructive coercions when validation_mode==permissive (e.g., string->int parse if digits-only) and return COERCION_APPLIED warnings.
- If a parameter is removed in newer manifests, include a compat_rules entry: {"removed":"old_param","fallback":"new_param","transform":"copy"} to allow automatic mapping. If transform fails, return DEPRECATED_PARAM warning with suggested_fixes.

Acceptance criteria (tests):
- Unit test suite covers each canonical error code with both strict and permissive modes.
- End-to-end test that streaming tool calls propagate validation errors early in the streaming handshake and surface the canonical error bundle as the first (non-stream) message chunk, with a stable envelope that SDKs can parse.
- SDK mapping documented: map MISSING_REQUIRED & TYPE_MISMATCH -> user-visible field-level errors; UNKNOWN_PARAMETER -> optional logging + console warning; COERCION_APPLIED -> debug log only.
- Console: param-level inline error message and link to manifest docs. Traces: validation_result must be attached to trace span as JSON.

Operational notes:
- Validation must be cheap and cached: pre-compile validators per tool_id+manifest_version and cache compiled validators in memory keyed by manifest hash.
- Log level: validation failures that are severity==error should increment a metric redirection (tool.validation.errors) with labels for code and tool_id. Warnings increment tool.validation.warnings.

Open questions and trade-offs:
- How far to push coercion? Too aggressive coercion hides client bugs. Recommendation: permissive mode only for internal/backwards-compat flows with explicit opt-in.
- Should we adopt full JSON Schema to avoid reimplementing semantics? That increases manifest complexity and makes manifests less authorable for customers. The lightweight DSL keeps manifests readable for partners.

Follow-ups (after this ticket):
- Design SDK error mapping and internationalization of short_message strings.
- Add a small compat-testing harness that replays historical manifests to detect breaking changes automatically.

2025-02-18 - Diego Ramos: Prototype validator implemented in a branch. Used a thin Ajv-based translator for the DSL to runtime rules. Early results: coercion path needs stricter controls to avoid silent truncation of floats to ints.

2025-02-21 - Maya Chen: UX review notes from Console team - prefer error codes to be stable strings and not contain slashes. Added acceptance criterion for streaming behavior: errors must be sent prior to any token stream.
2025-02-24 - Diego Ramos: Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4782 - implements manifest parser and in-memory validator cache. Needs tests for pattern/regression with unicode input.

2025-02-26 - Security review (notes): Require manifest_version and tool_id be signed in Private deployments to prevent manifest injection. Recorded in ticket; will require KMS-backed signing in a follow-up.

2025-03-01 - QA (Simone Ortiz): Added integration test plan to validate SDK behavior on unknown params and coercion warnings. Observed one edge-case where array items are coerced from comma-separated strings; marked as bug.
